sourceType: Current primary documentation retrieved through web tool

results.verified: Client-credentials grant uses an installed app in the same Shopify organization as the shop. The form POST endpoint is /admin/oauth/access_token. Response fields are access_token, scope, expires_in; documented expiry is 86399 seconds. Scope reflects installed app-version access, not narrowing in the token request.
results.implication: A dedicated approved app and actual returned-scope proof remain necessary. A static short-lived token alone does not establish durable cloud authentication.

results.verified: read_products maps to Product/ProductVariant; read_markets to Market; read_locales to ShopLocale; read_translations to Translation/TranslatableResource; read_metaobjects to Metaobject. A write scope includes read authority, so write access must not be added merely to satisfy an aggregated query validator.
results.implication: The six-scope allowlist is restricted to relevant read families, with read_publications corroborated separately. It is a permission ceiling, not proof that every subset can execute the collector.

results.verified: Retrieved the current official publications reference; read_publications is the relevant documented read scope.
Retrieved the official Metaobject reference for the collector taxonomy-reference field family.
results.implication: No Metaobject definition writes or definition scope is needed by the exact collector query.

results.verified: Current docs state Free per-invocation subrequests 50 and internal-service subrequests 1000; redirects can add subrequests. Variable size is stated as 5 KB. Memory is 128 MB and platform plan/CPU constraints remain separate.
results.implication: The observed 41 external fetch case leaves external-request headroom; R2/Queue accounting is distinct. Initial 5092-byte config is too close to the stated variable boundary, so the primary agent is separating bindings and requiring exact reconstruction.

results.verified: Current queue documentation gives a 15-minute consumer wall-clock limit and separate CPU limits.
results.implication: Reader token validity must cover the complete possible consumer duration, not only a 60-second margin at reader construction.
